prompt: Create logo.svg in this folder: a square 256x256 logo with a dark background (#0A0C11), a mint accent (#7CF5C8), and a geometric mark built from at least three shapes. It must be valid SVG that renders. Then write colors.md listing every hex colour you used and what each one is for.

assertions.value:
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
root = ET.parse('logo.svg').getroot()
tag = root.tag.split('}')[-1]
assert tag == 'svg', f'root element is {tag}, not svg'
ns = {'s': 'http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'}
shapes = root.findall('.//s:rect', ns) + root.findall('.//s:circle', ns) + root.findall('.//s:polygon', ns) + root.findall('.//s:path', ns) + root.findall('.//s:ellipse', ns)
assert len(shapes) >= 3, f'only {len(shapes)} shapes, asked for at least three'
text = open('logo.svg', encoding='utf-8').read()
assert '#0A0C11' in text.upper(), 'the requested background colour is missing'
assert '#7CF5C8' in text.upper(), 'the requested mint accent is missing'
print('OK')
assertions.evidence_note: the SVG parses as XML, has an svg root, carries three or more drawable shapes, and uses both requested colours -- parsed rather than eyeballed

assertions.value:
text = open('colors.md', encoding='utf-8').read().upper()
assert '#0A0C11' in text and '#7CF5C8' in text, 'colors.md does not list both colours in use'
assert len(text.strip()) > 40, 'colors.md is effectively empty'
print('OK')
assertions.evidence_note: an SVG alone does not document a palette; the second artifact must name the colours it used
